editorial:
If you have ever wanted to see Kate Beckinsale back in her black leather suit kicking serious butt, this fourth Underworld movie delivers exactly that. After years locked away in a lab, Selene wakes up to a world where humans have figured out that vampires and Lycans are real, and they are hunting both sides down. The story moves fast, throwing you straight into gunfights, explosions, and plenty of slow-motion action. It feels like a comic book come to life, with dark city streets, glowing eyes, and a whole lot of blood. Even if you missed the earlier films, you can still follow along because the movie explains enough to keep you moving. The vibe is pure adrenaline, and it rarely slows down long enough for you to catch your breath.

Kate Beckinsale carries the whole thing with her tough, no-nonsense energy, and the action scenes are the real highlight here. The special effects look sharp, especially the new super Lycans that are bigger and scarier than before. On the downside, the story is pretty thin and the dialogue can feel cheesy at times. Still, if you are in the mood for a fun, brain-off action ride, this one hits the spot. Fans of the series and anyone who enjoys monster battles will have a blast. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Selene discovers that the young girl Eve is actually her daughter, created from her blood during her imprisonment. The evil corporation Antigen has been experimenting on both of them. Selene teams up with a friendly Lycan named David to take down the company and its leader, Dr. Jacob Lane, who turns out to be a powerful Lycan himself. After a brutal final battle, Selene kills Lane and escapes with Eve and David. The movie ends with Selene vowing to hunt down the remaining Lycans and protect her daughter, setting up more adventures ahead.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves action-packed monster battles and strong female leads.
